items.title: Skeletal Ising fusion-data package
items.design_state: A-page local mathematical definition of exact Ising fusion channels, F-symbols and duality maps needed for the physical realization.
items.statement:
Let the scalar field be $\mathbb C$ and let the simple labels be $\mathbf 1$, $\psi$, and $\sigma$. Define a $\mathbb C$-linear semisimple category candidate whose objects are finite direct sums of these labels, whose simple-label Hom space is $\mathbb C$ when the labels agree and $0$ otherwise, and whose Hom spaces between direct sums are the corresponding finite matrices. Give the simple-label fusion product by

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi.
$$

Extend the product bilinearly to direct sums and on morphisms by the induced tensor product of scalar maps. The unit is $\mathbf 1$ and the unitors are strict. Fusion spaces are $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$; each is one-dimensional when the displayed fusion rule allows $c$ and is zero otherwise. In every allowed one-dimensional fusion space choose its displayed basis vector. On three simple labels, define the associator in these bases by the matrix $[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}$, where $x$ is the intermediate label in $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\to d$ and $y$ is the intermediate label in $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\to d$. Set

$$
\left[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}\right]_{xy}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}_{xy},\qquad x,y\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
\left[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad \left[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1.
$$

Every other coefficient is $1$ when all four fusion vertices are allowed and $0$ when any required fusion vertex is forbidden. Extend each associator linearly over direct sums. The candidate dual of each simple label is itself. For $\mathbf 1$ and $\psi$, take evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit-channel basis maps with coefficient $1$. For $\sigma$, take evaluation $\sigma\otimes\sigma\to\mathbf 1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf 1\to\sigma\otimes\sigma$ to have coefficient $2^{1/4}$ in the $\mathbf 1$ channel and zero in the $\psi$ channel. This item specifies the data; the separate coherence result checks that they satisfy the fusion-category axioms. No braiding or physical realization is included in this definition.

items.title: Coherence of the Ising fusion data
items.design_state: A-page local mathematical coherence result with an exact exhaustive pentagon check; no physical premises.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal I$ be the following complex-linear category. An object is a triple $X=(H_{\mathbf 1},H_\psi,H_\sigma)$ of finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces; a morphism $f:X\to Y$ is a triple of linear maps $f_a:H_a\to K_a$, with componentwise composition. For $a\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma\}$, let $\underline a$ be the triple with component $\mathbb C$ in position $a$ and zero in the other two positions. A zero object is an object with a unique morphism to and from every object. A monomorphism $u:Y\to X$ is a morphism such that $u\circ f=u\circ g$ implies $f=g$ for every object $Z$ and maps $f,g:Z\to Y$; a subobject of $X$ is an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $X$. An object is simple if it is nonzero and its only subobjects are the zero subobject and itself. The objects $\underline{\mathbf 1},\underline\psi,\underline\sigma$ are the three simple labels, and every object is a finite direct sum of them. The tensor product on these labels is

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi,
$$

and extends to arbitrary objects by orthogonal direct sums and to morphisms by tensor products of their component maps. More explicitly, if $Y=(K_{\mathbf 1},K_\psi,K_\sigma)$, then $(X\otimes Y)_c=\bigoplus_{a,b}H_a\otimes K_b\otimes V_{ab}^c$, where $V_{ab}^c=\mathbb C$ with its unit basis vector when the fusion rule allows $c$, and $V_{ab}^c=0$ otherwise. Put $N_{ab}^c=\dim_{\mathbb C}V_{ab}^c$, so $N_{ab}^c$ is $1$ for an allowed channel and $0$ otherwise. The unit object is $\underline{\mathbf 1}$. The left unitor on the unique summand $\mathbb C\otimes H_a\otimes V_{\mathbf 1a}^a$ is $z\otimes v\otimes u_{\mathbf 1a}^a\mapsto zv$; the right unitor on $H_a\otimes\mathbb C\otimes V_{a\mathbf 1}^a$ is $v\otimes z\otimes u_{a\mathbf 1}^a\mapsto zv$. Here $u_{ab}^c$ is the chosen unit fusion basis vector. These canonical unitors are specified isomorphisms, not literal equalities of Hilbert spaces; they realize the skeletal package's strict unit convention in this Hilbert-space presentation. For each allowed one-dimensional fusion space choose this unit basis vector. On simple labels the associator from $(a\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $a\otimes(b\otimes c)$ has coefficients $[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}$, where $x$ and $y$ are respectively the left and right intermediate labels. Set $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$, and specify

$$
[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{xy}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(-1)^{\epsilon(x)\epsilon(y)},\qquad x,y\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad [F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1.
$$

Every other coefficient is $1$ if all four fusion vertices are allowed and is $0$ otherwise. For general triples $X=(H_a)$, $Y=(K_b)$, $Z=(L_c)$, the associator sends the left-channel elementary tensor

$$
(v\otimes w\otimes u_{ab}^{x})\otimes z\otimes u_{xc}^{d}\ \longmapsto\ \sum_y[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}\,v\otimes(w\otimes z\otimes u_{bc}^{y})\otimes u_{ay}^{d},
$$

where $v\in H_a$, $w\in K_b$, $z\in L_c$, and the sum ranges over allowed channels. Extend this formula complex-linearly to every orthogonal direct-sum block. It includes the ordinary reassociation of the three Hilbert-space factors and moves no multiplicity vector between different labels.

For each simple label $a$, both chosen left and right dual labels are $a$. The four evaluation and coevaluation maps for $a$ have coefficient $\lambda_a$ in the unique unit channel, where $\lambda_{\mathbf 1}=\lambda_\psi=1$ and $\lambda_\sigma=2^{1/4}$; for $a=\sigma$ the coefficient in the $\psi$ channel is zero. For a general object $X=(H_a)_{a\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma\}}$, set $X^L=X^R=(H_a^*)_a$, where $H_a^*$ is the linear dual equipped with its dual Hilbert inner product. The evaluation maps pair $x\otimes\varphi$ or $\varphi\otimes x$ as $\lambda_a\varphi(x)$ in the $a\otimes a\to\mathbf 1$ channel, and vanish between different simple labels. For any basis $(e_{a,r})_r$ of each $H_a$ with dual basis $(e_{a,r}^*)_r$, the right coevaluation is $\sum_a\lambda_a\sum_r e_{a,r}^*\otimes e_{a,r}$ and the left coevaluation is $\sum_a\lambda_a\sum_r e_{a,r}\otimes e_{a,r}^*$, each in the $a\otimes a\to\mathbf 1$ channel.

Equip the category with the dagger $f^\dagger=(f_a^\dagger)_a$, where $f_a^\dagger$ is the Hilbert-space adjoint, and with the positive Hermitian inner products

$$
\langle f,g\rangle_{X,Y}=\sum_{a\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma\}}d_a\,\operatorname{Tr}(f_a^\dagger g_a),\qquad d_{\mathbf 1}=d_\psi=1,\quad d_\sigma=\sqrt2,
$$

on each $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal I}(X,Y)$. Composition-adjoint means $\langle g\circ f,h\rangle_{X,Z}=\langle f,g^\dagger\circ h\rangle_{X,Y}$ for $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and $h:X\to Z$. Tensor compatibility means $(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$ and $\langle f\otimes g,f'\otimes g'\rangle=\langle f,f'\rangle\langle g,g'\rangle$ for parallel pairs of maps. A morphism is unitary when its dagger is its two-sided inverse. Here “unitary fusion category” means that all Hom spaces are finite-dimensional; the three $\underline a$ are exactly the simple isomorphism classes and every object is a finite direct sum of them; the component categories have kernels and cokernels and every subspace has a complement; the bilinear tensor product has unit $\mathbf 1$, its associator is a natural isomorphism satisfying the pentagon, and its specified canonical unitors satisfy the triangle; every object has the stated left and right dual maps satisfying the two snakes; and the dagger and Hom inner products are positive and composition-adjoint, the tensor product satisfies the stated compatibilities, the left evaluation is adjoint to the right coevaluation, the right evaluation is adjoint to the left coevaluation, and the associator and unitors are unitary. These data satisfy all of these conditions.

items.title: Finite-lattice realization of the Ising non-invertible defect
items.design_state: Assigned conditional finite-lattice physical theorem with explicit Hamiltonian, defect operator, fusion and junction data.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $L\ge2$ and the periodic site set $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$. Let $\mathcal H_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ with orthonormal basis $|h_1,\ldots,h_L\rangle$, where every $h_j\in\mathbb Z_2$ and $h_0=h_L$. Define Pauli operators by $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Adopt the finite quantum Ising model with Hamiltonian

$$
H_L=-J\sum_{j=1}^{L}(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j),\qquad J>0,
$$

where $Z_{L+1}=Z_1$, $J$ has units of energy, and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through a time interval $s\ge0$ is the exact finite matrix $e^{-sH_L}$, with $s$ in inverse-energy units. Correlators are matrix elements between arbitrary boundary vectors of finite ordered lists of observable matrices and these propagation factors.

Let $\widehat{\mathcal H}_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ have basis $|\widehat h_{1/2},\ldots,\widehat h_{L-1/2}\rangle$, with dual Pauli operators $\widehat Z$ and $\widehat X$ defined by the same formulas on half-integer sites. Define the original-to-dual Kramers–Wannier map $K_L:\mathcal H_L\to\widehat{\mathcal H}_L$ by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|K_L|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-L/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{L}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)}.
$$

The reverse-oriented map is $K_L^\dagger:\widehat{\mathcal H}_L\to\mathcal H_L$. To give a single endodefect with the fusion convention below, use the explicit reflection identification $R_L:\widehat{\mathcal H}_L\to\mathcal H_L$ sending $|\widehat{\mathbf h}\rangle$ to $|\mathbf r\rangle$ with $r_j=\widehat h_{1/2-j}$ (all indices are periodic), and set $D_L=R_LK_L$. This is an isometry of the two spin bases and identifies the dual Hamiltonian with $H_L$. The matrix of $D_L$ is real symmetric: its exponent is $\sum_j r_{1-j}(h_{j-1}+h_j)$, whose coefficient matrix is symmetric in $\mathbf r$ and $\mathbf h$. Thus $D_L^2=K_L^\dagger K_L$. The original-to-dual map and its reverse also have the typed fusion $K_L^\dagger K_L=I+P_L$ and $K_LK_L^\dagger=I+\widehat P_L$. A repeated fixed half-site identification is not used for this square; it would retain a spatial translation. A defect line is a wrapping insertion of $D_L$ on a Euclidean time slice. Its allowed position changes are slides within gaps between fixed observable insertions. In this finite lattice model, topologicality means invariance under the declared local line slides; re-association of junction channels is a separate linear recoupling identity; no smooth continuum isotopy claim is made. A finite defect network has labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, represented on the chain by $I,P_L,D_L$, where $P_L=\prod_jX_j$. Its fusion spaces are one-dimensional precisely for

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi,
$$

and zero otherwise. Choose a basis vector in each allowed one-dimensional fusion space and define the associator in those bases as follows. Write $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$; then

$$
[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)},\qquad a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad [F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,
$$

and every other allowed associator coefficient is $1$. In the abstract channel category, the unit maps $\mathbf 1\otimes a\to a$ and $a\otimes\mathbf 1\to a$ have coefficient $1$. Each simple label is self-dual; its left and right evaluation and coevaluation maps have coefficient $\lambda_a$ in the unit channel, where $\lambda_{\mathbf 1}=\lambda_\psi=1$ and $\lambda_\sigma=2^{1/4}$, with zero coefficient in the $\psi$ channel for $\sigma\otimes\sigma$. These are categorical maps, distinct from the lattice triangle normalizations below.

For local lattice tensors, heights $h,h',\widetilde h$ range over $\mathbb Z_2$, with addition modulo $2$; height $0$ denotes the label $\mathbf 1$, height $1$ denotes $\psi$, and a vertex marked $\sigma$ denotes an empty site. Set $Q_{hh'}=\delta_{h',h+1}$. The two nontrivial height placements of a trivalent junction of two $\sigma$ lines and one $\psi$ line have the following weights: when the vertex between the two $\sigma$ lines has ordinary height $h$ and the other vertices are empty, the weight is $T_{\sigma\sigma\psi}(h)$; when that vertex is empty and the other two have ordinary heights $h,h'$, the weight is $T_{\sigma\psi\sigma}(h,h')$. Explicitly,

$$
T_{\sigma\sigma\psi}(h)=2^{-1/4}(-1)^h,\qquad T_{\sigma\psi\sigma}(h,h')=Q_{hh'}.
$$

The identity-defect termination tensors have the following four orientations: the first two represent the two local orientations of the $\sigma\otimes\sigma\to\mathbf 1$ unit channel, and the last two represent the two local orientations of the $\psi\otimes\psi\to\mathbf 1$ unit channel. In each case the dashed third edge has label $\mathbf 1$ and the two sloping defect edges have the indicated common label:

- For defect label $\sigma$, when the upper vertex has height $h$ and the two lower vertices are empty sites, the tensor is $2^{-1/4}$.
- For defect label $\sigma$, when the upper vertex is empty and the lower vertices have heights $h,h'$, the tensor is $\delta_{hh'}$.
- For defect label $\psi$, when all three site vertices are empty, the tensor is $2^{-1/4}$.
- For defect label $\psi$, when the upper vertex has dual height $\widetilde h$ and the lower vertices have heights $h,h'$, the tensor is $Q_{h\widetilde h}\delta_{hh'}$.

In the last orientation, $\widetilde h$ is the upper dual-basis height and $h,h'$ are the lower ordinary heights, all in $\mathbb Z_2$. The mixed index $Q_{h\widetilde h}$ uses the same $h$ as $\delta_{hh'}$; there is no second independent dual height. Reversed orientations use adjoint tensors; every fusion-forbidden label or height assignment has weight zero, and all components outside the stated domains are zero. The other allowed channels use their unit basis maps of coefficient $1$. These local triangles and the abstract channel maps above are the adopted junction data of this finite network model, not consequences of the fusion multiplicities alone.

The complete admissible input domain is declared as follows. Each input is a finite decorated lattice tensor network with boundary vectors or boundary tensors, arbitrary finite ordinary insertion matrices, propagation tensors $e^{-sH_L}$ (or their dual versions), and any finite number of the wrapping defects and local trivalent junction tensors above, with their oriented site orderings. Local height edges have index set $\{0,1\}$, empty-site edges have the singleton label $\sigma$, and row edges have index set $\mathbb Z_2^L$. Matching edges are contracted only when their index sets and model sides agree; reversal uses the stated adjoint tensor. Boundary vectors and all uncontracted indices are part of the combined boundary data. The correlator is the unnormalized complex number

$$
C(\Gamma;b;O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\sum_{\text{internal admissible indices}}\left(\prod_v d_v\right)\left(\prod_{t\in\Gamma}\mathcal T_t(\text{incident indices})\right),\qquad d_v=\begin{cases}1,&\text{ordinary spin site},\\\sqrt2,&\text{empty site}.\end{cases}
$$

Here the finite graph $\Gamma$ records all sites, incidences, side labels, tensor orientations, and the external boundary contraction; $\mathcal T_t$ is exactly the specified matrix component or local triangle component at $t$. The product over $v$ runs over local patch sites whose factors are not already absorbed into a row tensor; row matrices have their displayed normalization. Every site weight is included once; if a site is split among patches, its positive factors are split with product $d_v$. Unit defect quadrilaterals carry $2^{-1/4}\delta_{a\alpha}\delta_{b\beta}$, and a duality quadrilateral carries $2^{-1/2}(-1)^{ab}$ at its two ordinary corners; forbidden assignments vanish. These give a fully finite contraction prescription, including the source's site-weight convention, rather than inferring network correlators from fusion multiplicities. On a row with no extra local junction patch it is exactly the ordered matrix element already specified. Reflection identifications permute the row and boundary indices consistently and do not change a contraction. The value space is $\mathbb C$ with its usual topology. A declared line slide moves an entire $I$, $P_L$ or $D_L$ slice within a gap containing no other tensor insertion, leaving all boundary tensors fixed. Junction recouplings compare the two local contractions with the same external height indices, including site factors; equality or a specified linear combination must hold before the rest of the graph is contracted. No arbitrary continuum network or additional support deformation is asserted.

For this selected finite model, $D_L$ is topological under the declared defect slides, its exact operator fusion is $D_L^2=I+P_L$, $P_L^2=I$, and $D_LP_L=P_LD_L=D_L$, and the junction spaces and associators are the finite semisimple unitary Ising fusion data above. In particular $D_L$ is non-invertible. The claim is confined to this finite lattice model and asserts no continuum limit or empirical fact.

title: Non-Invertible Symmetry Operators and Fusion — Examples

items.title: The Ising fusion object is simple and non-invertible
items.design_state: B-page abstract finite algebraic example using the exact local mathematical suppliers; no physical-realization claim.
items.statement:
A zero object is an object that is both initial and terminal. A monomorphism $u:Y\to X$ is a morphism such that, for every object $Z$ and morphisms $f,g:Z\to Y$, $u\circ f=u\circ g$ implies $f=g$. A subobject of $X$ is an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $X$, and $X$ is simple if it is nonzero and has no subobjects other than the zero subobject and $X$ itself. Let $\mathcal I$ have as objects finite direct sums of the labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$. Its bilinear tensor product on labels is

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi.
$$

Morphisms are block-diagonal across the three labels, with an arbitrary finite complex matrix on each equal-label block and zero on unequal-label blocks; composition is blockwise matrix multiplication. Each label is simple by the stated criterion. The tensor product is bilinear, the unit is $\mathbf 1$, and the unitors are strict. Choose one basis vector in each allowed one-dimensional fusion space. An object $X$ is tensor-invertible if some object $E$ satisfies both $X\otimes E\cong\mathbf 1$ and $E\otimes X\cong\mathbf 1$; otherwise it is non-invertible. A right tensor inverse of $\sigma$ means an object $E$ with $\sigma\otimes E\cong\mathbf 1$. Encode intermediate labels by $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$. The associator $\alpha_{a,b,c}:(a\otimes b)\otimes c\to a\otimes(b\otimes c)$ has coefficients $[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)}$ for $a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\}$, $[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1$, and $[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1$; every other coefficient is $1$ when all required fusion channels are allowed and $0$ otherwise. Since $\sigma$ has no right tensor inverse, it has no two-sided tensor inverse and is non-invertible. This is an abstract algebraic example and makes no physical-realization claim.

items.title: A non-invertible defect on a three-site Ising ring
items.design_state: B-page exact three-site finite-Hamiltonian example of a topological non-invertible defect; no continuum or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H_3=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^3)$ with orthonormal basis $|h_1,h_2,h_3\rangle$, and define $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Use periodic indices and the finite Hamiltonian $H_3=-J\sum_{j=1}^3(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j)$, where $J>0$ has energy units and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through $s\ge0$ is $e^{-sH_3}$. Define $K_3$ from this ring to its half-shifted dual by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|K_3|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-3/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{3}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)},\qquad h_0=h_3,
$$

and use the supplier's reflection identification $R_3|\widehat{\mathbf h}\rangle=|\mathbf r\rangle$, $r_j=\widehat h_{1/2-j}$, to set $D_3=R_3K_3$. Its complete admissible defect-bearing correlators are exactly the finite decorated tensor contractions, ordinary insertions and external boundary tensors of the supplier at $L=3$; allowed slides keep the rest of that complete input fixed. Let $P_3=X_1X_2X_3$ and $v=|000\rangle-|111\rangle$. The defect inserted on a Euclidean time slice is topological under the declared slides within gaps of fixed insertions, satisfies $D_3^2=I+P_3$, and annihilates $v$ after two fusions. Therefore this exact finite-model defect is non-invertible. No continuum or empirical claim is made.
